title: Boogie-Woogie book and Black Music History in schools
summary: On tape 4 he describes his book for E. B. Marks and plans to introduce black music history into New York schools.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: And then you did a book for...

Edward B. Marks, yeah, called In Boogie-Woogie Land. And I played some original tunes and have a sketch to show the illustrations and demonstrations. But what I wanted to do more than anything, and I'm going to be in touch with the Congressman from this District and his assistant to see if we can't induce the New York School System to introduce in their curriculum Black Music History, with Duke and Louis and myself and others, and so that when a kid go to the music class and hear Copland, he can hear Duke. He can hear Meade Lux Lewis. He can hear...what's this harmonica player, Larry Adler and he can hear Little Walter. And I'm hoping that I'll be able to get...if I can get one school district to do it, you know, I know that if, several

years ago we got them to invite an astronaut to come to Harlem, which they did, and gave the black kids an opportunity to see a black astronaut and to know that a black man can be involved in the space program.
